args.sql:
SELECT
  p.category,
  COUNT(*) AS items_delivered,
  COUNTIF(oi.status = 'Returned') AS items_returned,
  ROUND(COUNTIF(oi.status = 'Returned') / COUNT(*), 4) AS return_rate
FROM order_items AS oi
JOIN products AS p ON p.id = oi.product_id
WHERE p.brand = 'Carhartt'
  AND oi.status IN ('Complete', 'Returned')
GROUP BY p.category
HAVING items_delivered >= 50
ORDER BY return_rate DESC

# Q3 2026 Performance Review and Q4 Action Plan

## Executive summary
- Net revenue for your premium denim brands reached $45,068.36 in Q3 2026, representing a 41.7% increase compared to Q2 2026 ($31,792.65) and an 88.3% increase year-over-year against Q3 2025 ($23,938.77).
- Growth was driven by an expanding customer base and higher order volume, particularly in core Jeans and Shorts categories, while average order value remained stable.
- Search acquisition dominated performance, accounting for nearly 70% of total revenue.

## Key findings
- **Strong Revenue Expansion**: Q3 2026 net revenue grew to $45,068.36 across 266 orders, up from $31,792.65 (191 orders) in Q2 2026 and $23,938.77 (139 orders) in Q3 2025.
- **Stable Average Order Value**: Average order value (AOV) was $169.43 in Q3 2026, compared to $166.45 in Q2 2026 and $172.22 in Q3 2025.
- **Category Concentration**: The **Jeans** category generated $34,043.30 (75.5% of total net revenue) across 675 units sold, followed by **Shorts** at $3,610.89 and **Pants** at $2,467.63.
- **Customer Acquisition Mix**: New customers accounted for 262 buyers and $44,585.40 in net revenue, whereas returning customers generated just 4 orders and $482.96.
- **Traffic Source Performance**: **Search** was the primary revenue driver with $31,421.51 across 182 orders, followed by **Organic** ($5,829.60), **Display** ($3,080.42), **Facebook** ($2,762.96), and **Email** ($1,973.87).
- **Return Rates**: Overall return rates for core categories remained manageable: **Jeans** recorded a 9.1% return rate (23 returns out of 253 items) and **Shorts** 8.9% (4 returns out of 45 items). Higher return rates appeared in smaller volume categories such as **Tops & Tees** (37.5%) and **Maternity** (50.0%).

## Why it happened
- **Order Volume Growth**: The 39.3% quarter-over-quarter rise in order count (from 191 in Q2 to 266 in Q3) was the primary driver of revenue growth, supported by a large influx of first-time buyers.
- **Seasonal Demand Shift**: Sales in Shorts rose to $3,610.89 in Q3 from $3,099.05 in Q2 and $1,040.19 in Q3 2025, reflecting seasonal consumer demand during the summer months. *(Hypothesis to verify: warmer weather drove higher conversion on denim shorts).*
- **Acquisition Channel Efficiency**: Search traffic captured the vast majority of demand, indicating effective search engine marketing for premium denim brands. Retention channels (Email, Facebook) contributed lower volume, pointing to an opportunity to improve repeat purchase rates.

## Action items

| Action | Owner | Priority | Expected impact |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Scale paid search campaigns and keyword optimization for core denim lines | Marketing | High | Capture peak Q4 holiday shopping demand and maintain top-of-funnel customer acquisition growth |
| Launch targeted email marketing retention flows for Q3 first-time buyers | Marketing / CRM | High | Increase repeat customer rate (currently under 2% of Q3 buyers) ahead of the holiday season |
| Review sizing and product descriptions for high-return categories (Tops & Tees, Maternity) | Merchandising | Medium | Reduce return rates in secondary categories and protect operating margins |
| Expand inventory depth on top-performing Jeans fits and washes for Q4 | Supply Chain / Merchandising | High | Prevent stockouts during the high-volume fourth-quarter shopping period |

## Method and caveats
- **Data Scope**: Analysis covers orders and items for brands 7 For All Mankind, True Religion, Joe's Jeans, and AG Adriano Goldschmied. Figures exclude cancelled and returned items.
- **Definitions**: 
  - Net revenue = $\sum$ (sale_price) for items with status other than Cancelled or Returned.
  - AOV = Net revenue / total distinct orders.
  - Return rate = Returned items / total ordered items in category.
- **Period**: Q3 2026 (July 1 – September 30, 2026), compared against Q2 2026 and Q3 2025. Timestamps are UTC.

---

  COUNT(DISTINCT oi.order_id) AS orders,
  ROUND(SUM(oi.sale_price), 2) AS net_revenue
FROM order_items AS oi
JOIN products AS p ON p.id = oi.product_id
JOIN users AS u ON u.id = oi.user_id
WHERE oi.status NOT IN ('Cancelled', 'Returned')
  AND p.brand IN ('7 For All Mankind', 'True Religion', "Joe's Jeans", 'AG Adriano Goldschmied')
  AND DATE(oi.created_at) BETWEEN '2026-07-01' AND '2026-09-30'
GROUP BY u.traffic_source
ORDER BY net_revenue DESC

# Q3 2026 Performance Review and Q4 Action Plan

## Executive summary
- Net revenue for your premium denim brands reached $45,068.36 in Q3 2026, representing a 41.7% increase compared to Q2 2026 ($31,792.65) and an 88.3% increase year-over-year against Q3 2025 ($23,938.77).
- Growth was driven by an expanding customer base and higher order volume, particularly in core Jeans and Shorts categories, while average order value remained stable.
- Search acquisition dominated performance, accounting for nearly 70% of total revenue.

## Key findings
- **Strong Revenue Expansion**: Q3 2026 net revenue grew to $45,068.36 across 266 orders, up from $31,792.65 (191 orders) in Q2 2026 and $23,938.77 (139 orders) in Q3 2025.
- **Stable Average Order Value**: Average order value (AOV) was $169.43 in Q3 2026, compared to $166.45 in Q2 2026 and $172.22 in Q3 2025.
- **Category Concentration**: The **Jeans** category generated $34,043.30 (75.5% of total net revenue) across 675 units sold, followed by **Shorts** at $3,610.89 and **Pants** at $2,467.63.
- **Customer Acquisition Mix**: New customers accounted for 262 buyers and $44,585.40 in net revenue, whereas returning customers generated just 4 orders and $482.96.
- **Traffic Source Performance**: **Search** was the primary revenue driver with $31,421.51 across 182 orders, followed by **Organic** ($5,829.60), **Display** ($3,080.42), **Facebook** ($2,762.96), and **Email** ($1,973.87).
- **Return Rates**: Overall return rates for core categories remained manageable: **Jeans** recorded a 9.1% return rate (23 returns out of 253 items) and **Shorts** 8.9% (4 returns out of 45 items). Higher return rates appeared in smaller volume categories such as **Tops & Tees** (37.5%) and **Maternity** (50.0%).

## Why it happened
- **Order Volume Growth**: The 39.3% quarter-over-quarter rise in order count (from 191 in Q2 to 266 in Q3) was the primary driver of revenue growth, supported by a large influx of first-time buyers.
- **Seasonal Demand Shift**: Sales in Shorts rose to $3,610.89 in Q3 from $3,099.05 in Q2 and $1,040.19 in Q3 2025, reflecting seasonal consumer demand during the summer months. *(Hypothesis to verify: warmer weather drove higher conversion on denim shorts).*
- **Acquisition Channel Efficiency**: Search traffic captured the vast majority of demand, indicating effective search engine marketing for premium denim brands. Retention channels (Email, Facebook) contributed lower volume, pointing to an opportunity to improve repeat purchase rates.

## Action items

| Action | Owner | Priority | Expected impact |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Scale paid search campaigns and keyword optimization for core denim lines | Marketing | High | Capture peak Q4 holiday shopping demand and maintain top-of-funnel customer acquisition growth |
| Launch targeted email marketing retention flows for Q3 first-time buyers | Marketing / CRM | High | Increase repeat customer rate (currently under 2% of Q3 buyers) ahead of the holiday season |
| Review sizing and product descriptions for high-return categories (Tops & Tees, Maternity) | Merchandising | Medium | Reduce return rates in secondary categories and protect operating margins |
| Expand inventory depth on top-performing Jeans fits and washes for Q4 | Supply Chain / Merchandising | High | Prevent stockouts during the high-volume fourth-quarter shopping period |

## Method and caveats
- **Data Scope**: Analysis covers orders and items for brands 7 For All Mankind, True Religion, Joe's Jeans, and AG Adriano Goldschmied. Figures exclude cancelled and returned items.
- **Definitions**: 
  - Net revenue = $\sum$ (sale_price) for items with status other than Cancelled or Returned.
  - AOV = Net revenue / total distinct orders.
  - Return rate = Returned items / total ordered items in category.
- **Period**: Q3 2026 (July 1 – September 30, 2026), compared against Q2 2026 and Q3 2025. Timestamps are UTC.
